glosses: A substance used to polish.

examples.text: A good silver polish will remove tarnish easily.

examples.text: The floor was waxed to a high polish.

glosses: Refinement; cleanliness in performance or presentation.

examples.text: The lecturer showed a lot of polish at his last talk.

glosses: To shine; to make a surface very smooth or shiny by rubbing, cleaning, or grinding.

examples.text: He polished up the chrome until it gleamed.

glosses: To refine; remove imperfections from.

examples.text: The band has polished its performance since the last concert.

examples.text: Steel polishes well.

examples.text: If there was a sharp point nearby, electricity would stream from it in a luminous brush, a little corposant, and one could blow out candles with the outstreaming “electric wind,” or even get this to turn a little rotor on its pivot.

examples.text: The water shone pacifically; the sky, without a speck, was a benign immensity of unstained light; the very mist on the Essex marshes was like a gauzy and radiant fabric, hung from the wooded rises inland, and draping the low shores in diaphanous folds.
